name: Steppe
desc: A grass sea under a supercell — the storm base turns overhead on its own slow rotation with a rain curtain trailing out of it, a bright slot of clear sky burns along the horizon underneath, and gust fronts comb the plain in broad pale bands that run away to the haze while the cloud shadow crawls across and drags the light with it; storm green, sumi ink wash, a dust-bowl ochre drought, a cyan met-chart schematic, or thermal false-colour.

energy.doc: how hard the storm is working — sunlit cloud flanks, rain-curtain density, depth of the cloud shadow on the plain

scale.doc: size of the near grass — at max, blades stand up the whole frame and you are down in it

density.doc: how much foreground grass, rain and distant birds populate the plain

speed.doc: weather advection rate — how fast the cell tracks, the gusts run and the rain falls

wind.doc: how hard it is blowing — gust-front contrast on the plain and how far the near blades lie over

hue.doc: grass hue; the storm keys off its complement

x.doc: where the cell sits across the sky

y.doc: horizon as a canvas fraction — low horizon gives the sky to the storm, high gives the frame to the grass

style.doc: aesthetic: a green-black supercell over lit grass / sumi ink wash, the storm as tonal washes and the plain as dry-brush / a dust-bowl ochre drought where the rain never lands / a cyan meteorological chart of the cell, schematic and clinical / thermal false-colour, the cold core over a warm plain

seed.doc: weather lottery — cloud structure, gust pattern, grass layout
